DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http://wwvv.dilg.com.ph DILG OPINION No. 96 s. 2021 19 July 2021 HON. PEDRO M. ONG, JR. Vice Mayor Municipality of Baler, Aurora Dear Vice-Mayor Ong: This has reference to your letter dated 01 February 2021 requesting for this Department's opinion on the following issues, and we quote: "I.Whether or Not the Sangguniang Bayan (SB) may enact its own ordinance with a penal provision different from that of an existing Sangguniang Panlalawigan (SP) ordinance involving the same subject matter; 2. Whether or Not the SP erred in applying the Indeterminate Sentence Law (ISLAW) in the penal provision of the subject SP ordinance; and 3. Whether or Not the SB has authority to impose accessory penalties in addition to its power to impose administrative fine and/or imprisonment provided for by the Local Government Code. Per the documents submitted to the Central Office, it appears that you have presented the above-mentioned queries before the Sangguniang Panlalawigan of Aurora on 07 September 2020, wherein the SP in sum, opined that: • The SB can either adopt an existing provincial ordinance or enact its own ordinance, provided that it will only confine itself within the limits imposed under Article 447(1)(iii) of the Local Government Code (LGC); • ISLAW does not apply to an ordinance; • Section 16 of the LGC in relation to Section 447(1)(iii), provides that an LGU can impose the accessory penalty of confiscation, since it

is but a rational and logical consequence of preventing destructive fishing. Otherwise, the same paraphernalia can be used again for the same purpose; and • Implementing Rules and Regulations are not necessary for an ordinance to be effective. An ordinance can be implemented as long as it is clear and comprehensible. However, you hold the view that the foregoing opinion of the SP is ambiguous. Thus, you elevated the same to the Department for clarification. Please be informed that the Department concurs with the position of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan of Province of Aurora as the same is in accordance with the existing laws, rules and regulations. Nonetheless, may we further elaborate the same. With respect to the first issue, we answer in the affirmative. Pertinent to herein discussion is Section 447(a)(1 )(iii) and (vi) of Republic Act No. 7160, otherwise known as the "Local Govemment Code of 1991" (LGC) which provides that the Sangguniang Bayan (SB), being the local legislative body of the municipality, has the authority to enact ordinance(s) which protect the environment and impose penalties for acts which endanger the environment, such as destructive fishing. This is specified in Section 149 of the LGC which states that the sanggunian shall, by appropriate ordinance, penalize deleterious methods of fishing and prescribe a criminal penalty thereof in accordance with the LGC. Further, the sanggunian has the authority to prosecute any violation of the provisions of applicable fishery laws. Provided however, that the fine which can be imposed by the SB for violation of a municipal ordinance shall not exceed Two Thousand Five Hundred Pesos (P2,500.OO) or an imprisonment not exceeding six (6) months, or both in the discretion of the court. On the other hand, Section 458 (a)(l)(vi) of the LGC pertains to the power/authority of Sangguniang Panlalawigan to enact ordinances which protects the environment, including destructive fishing. Undoubtedly, the Sangguniang Bayan can enact its own ordinance with penal sanctions, different and separate from that of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan, provided the same is within the limits provided by the LGC as discussed above.

With respect to the second issue, we also answer in the affirmative. Pursuant to Section 1 of Act No. 4103, as amended by Act No. 4225 and Republic Act No. 4203, Indeterminate Sentence Law (ISLaw) applies only to offenses punished by the Revised Penal Code (RPC) and Special laws. Obviously, an ordinance is neither a special law nor a RPC. An ordinance is enacted by the sanggunian concerned, while both the RPC and special laws are enacted by the Congress. Clearly, ISLaw cannot be applied to the penalties which can be validly imposed by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan. Lastly, on the issue regarding the propriety of imposing accessory penalty of confiscation, we likewise answer in the affirmative. It must be noted that local government units shall exercise the powers which are expressly granted, those necessarily implied therefrom, as well as powers which are necessary, appropriate, or incidental for its efficient and effective governance, and those which are essential to the promotion of the general welfare. Inevitably, confiscation of paraphernalia that were used in illegal fishing activities, is but necessary and incidental for the efficient and effective implementation of the ordinance. Thus, we find no reason to deviate from the position of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan on the issues above mentioned. This opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. We hope to have assisted you accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: NGAN Underse retary for Local Government Ls/91/17
